title: Two Big Leaders Make a Deal About AI and Trade
summary:
What happens when the world's two biggest economies stop talking? That's what leaders wanted to fix this week. President Xi Jinping of China and President Donald Trump met in Washington for three days. When it was over, both countries said they would set up a special phone line for AI problems. That way, if something goes wrong with artificial intelligence, they can talk fast.

They also agreed to keep working on trade. Trump said China will buy 10 million metric tons of coal from the U.S. in 2027 and 2028. And they will keep talking about rare earths — special metals used in phones and computers.

Trump showed unusual warmth toward Xi, even though the two countries had been fighting about trade. But Trump also said the U.S. won't slow down its AI work. "We're leading by at least a year," he told reporters. "I'm not looking to open it up."

Both sides will meet again in November in Shenzhen, China, and later in Florida. It's not a giant breakthrough, but experts say talking is better than not talking.
why_it_matters: Many of the phones, computers, and games kids use are built with parts and metals from both countries, so when these leaders talk instead of fight, the things families buy can stay easier to get and less expensive.

background_read: Xi Jinping (China's top leader, who has been the country's president since 2013) and Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025) lead the two biggest economies on Earth.
For years, the United States and China have argued about trade, and both have charged extra taxes on goods coming from the other country.
Rare earths are special metals that mostly come from China, and phones, computers, and electric cars all need them.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Xi Jinping of China and President Donald Trump of the United States
WHAT: They met for three days and agreed to set up a special phone line for AI problems and to keep working on trade
WHERE: Washington, with more meetings planned in Shenzhen, China, and later in Florida
WHY: The two countries had stopped talking to each other, and experts say talking is better than not talking

perspectives.description: The two leaders met kindly and made plans to keep talking, which could mean fewer fights and lower prices on everyday things.
Experts say this is not a giant breakthrough, and Trump says the U.S. will not slow down its AI work at all.
Nothing is fully settled yet — the two sides only promised to keep talking at meetings coming up in November and later.
